content: Tolbutamide is an oral medication used to manage type 2 diabetes, a condition where the body does not use insulin effectively, leading to elevated blood sugar levels. It works by stimulating the pancreas to release insulin and improving the body’s ability to use insulin efficiently. However, it is only effective if the pancreas is capable of producing insulin. This medication is not suitable for treating type 1 diabetes, where the body does not produce insulin at all. In some cases, tolbutamide may be prescribed for other medical conditions; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Important Warning: Tolbutamide, like other oral hypoglycemic drugs, has been linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular-related mortality. It is essential to discuss with your doctor the potential risks, benefits, and alternative treatments before starting this medication. How to Use Tolbutamide: Tolbutamide is available in tablet form and is typically taken multiple times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take the medication exactly as prescribed—do not take more or less than directed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. Continue taking tolbutamide even if you feel well, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. Precautions Before Taking Tolbutamide: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to tolbutamide or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g. Notify your doctor if you have a history of heart or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking tolbutamide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking tolbutamide. Wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen when outdoors. Dietary Instructions: Follow the dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Maintain a healthy diet. Alcohol consumption may lower blood sugar levels, so consult your doctor about the safe use of alcoholic beverages while taking tolbutamide. Missed Dose: Before starting tolbutamide, ask your doctor what to do if you miss a dose, and write down these instructions for future reference. Generally, take the missed dose as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next dose. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: Tolbutamide may cause low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Your doctor will provide instructions on how to manage hypoglycemia, which may include checking your blood sugar levels, consuming sugary foods or drinks (e.g., hard candy or fruit juice), or seeking medical attention. Symptoms of hypoglycemia include: Shakiness Dizziness or lightheadedness Sweating Nervousness or irritability Sudden mood or behavior changes Headache Numbness or tingling around the mouth Weakness Pale skin Hunger Clumsy or jerky movements Severe Side Effects: If hypoglycemia is not treated, it can lead to severe symptoms. Confusion Seizures Loss of consciousness Hyperglycemia (high blood sugar) may also occur. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience: Extreme thirst Frequent urination Extreme hunger Weakness Blurred vision If untreated, hyperglycemia can lead to a life-threatening condition called diabetic ketoacidosis. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience: Dry mouth Nausea and vomiting Shortness of breath Fruity-smelling breath Decreased consciousness Other serious side effects of tolbutamide include: Skin rash, itching, or redness Severe sunburn Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) Light-colored stools Dark urine Unusual bleeding or bruising Fever or sore throat If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Storage Instructions: Store tolbutamide in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly—consult your pharmacist for guidance. Emergency/Overdose: In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Additional Information: Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order tests to monitor your response to tolbutamide and may instruct you on how to check your blood or urine sugar levels at home. Follow these instructions carefully. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Brand Name: Tolbutamide is sold under the brand name Orinase®.
